title: The Three Days Rule
cn: 第 21 集 · 三天规则
novel:
Ted and Barney [[debated|debate]] the "three days rule." The rule said you must wait three days before calling a woman after getting her number. Ted thought it was [[outdated|outdated]]. Barney thought it was [[sacred|sacred]].

Ted met a woman named Holly and got her number. He wanted to call immediately. "The three days rule is [[ridiculous|ridiculous]]," he said.

Barney was [[horrified|horrify]]. "You can't break the three days rule! It's [[tradition|tradition]]!"

So Ted [[compromised|compromise]]. He wouldn't call — he would text. But Marshall [[intercepted|intercept]] the texts. He started [[pretending|pretend]] to be Holly, texting Ted flirty messages.

Ted was [[thrilled|thrill]]. "She's so into me," he told the gang. He had no idea he was texting Marshall.

Marshall felt [[guilty|guilty]] but also [[amused|amuse]]. He [[escalated|escalate]] the flirting, making Ted increasingly [[confident|confident]] and [[ridiculous|ridiculous]].

Finally, Ted [[arranged|arrange]] a date with "Holly." When the real Holly showed up, she had no idea what Ted was talking about. "I never texted you," she said.

Ted was [[confused|confuse]]. Then Marshall [[confessed|confess]].

"It was me," Marshall said, [[hanging|hang]] his head.

Ted was [[furious|furious]]. "You [[pretended|pretend]] to be a girl?!"

"It was Barney's idea," Marshall [[blamed|blame]].

Barney [[shrugged|shrug]]. "The three days rule exists for a reason."

horrify.en: to make someone feel very shocked

tradition.en: something done for a long time

compromise.en: to reach agreement by giving up something

intercept.en: to stop something before it reaches its target

pretend.en: to act as if something is true

guilty.en: feeling bad about something you did

escalate.en: to make something bigger or more intense

confess.en: to tell the truth about something

hang.en: to let your head go down in shame

blame.en: to say someone is responsible for something bad

shrug.en: to raise your shoulders to show you don't care
